Agreement or concurrence of opinion, will, or action.

examples.text: These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Iesus, and with his brethen.

glosses: A harmony in sound, pitch and tone; concord.

examples.text: Those sweet accords are even the angels' lays.

glosses: Agreement or harmony of things in general.

examples.text: the accord of light and shade in painting

glosses: A distinctive mixture of fragrances or the odor thereof.

examples.text: Oriental fragrances often incorporate an accord referred to as amber. It is a perfumery accord using vanilla, olibanum, balsamic resins, and citrus to varying degrees.
Fougères are built on an accord between lavender and coumarin, with every conceivable variation and elaboration.
Accord is the perfumer's word for a perfume formulation that can be incorporated into any perfume calling for a particular note.

glosses: An agreement between parties in controversy, by which satisfaction for an injury is stipulated, and which, when executed, prevents a lawsuit.

examples.text: Accord is a satisfaction agreed upon between the party injuring and the party injured ; which , when performed , is a bar of all actions upon this account

glosses: An international agreement.

examples.text: The Geneva Accord of 1954 ended the French-Indochinese War.

glosses: Voluntary or spontaneous impulse to act.

examples.text: Nobody told me to do it. I did it of my own accord.

examples.text: [H]er hands accorded the Lutes muſicke to the voice; […]

glosses: To bring (people) to an agreement; to reconcile, settle, adjust or harmonize.
